title: Evals run plan
description: The frozen experiment: which dataset revision, which cases, which targets through which protocols, how many independent repeats, and the bounds the runner must obey. A plan is written before any review and hashed; a run records that hash so a continuation can prove it is finishing the same selection rather than a drifted one. Writing and checking a plan is offline: nothing here calls a model by itself, and only an explicit run command reaches a provider.

planBody.description: A plan's members. `caseIds` may be omitted on the authored document and is then resolved from `split` once, at run start; the run index stores the resolved list, which is what makes the selection frozen. Every other member is required, because a plan with an unstated bound is not a bound.

datasetPath.description: Repository-relative dataset directory, so a plan stays portable between checkouts holding the same revision.

split.description: Which split this plan selects. A split selects whole families, so two plans over the same dataset with different splits share no case.

caseIds.description: The cases to run. Omitted means the split decides, once, when the plan is resolved.

transport.description: offline replaces only the socket: the production renderer, parser, envelope rule, normalization and outcome mapping all still run. live is the same path against a real provider.

protocols.description: The protocols this experiment asks for. A target that does not support one of them leaves that grid cell unsupported rather than inventing a request for it.

repeats.description: Independent repeats of each case through each target and protocol. Each repeat is its own cell and its own review call, never a stored answer re-read as a second observation.

context.description: The input budget the snapshot is trimmed to, kept apart from the run's own token bound.

fixture.description: Path to the scripted socket an offline plan replays, relative to the plan document. A live plan has none, and an offline plan without one cannot run: replaying nothing is not the same as replaying a refusal.
